Maria G.: Quick follow-up on the RFC about cost attribution when attributes arrive late. We saw two customer tickets where billing_key was missing in the ingest envelope and the query team had trouble reconciling costs. Thoughts on a pragmatic fallback?

Ben T.: Thanks — we debated late-join vs early-resolve in the RFC. Short version: early-resolve simplifies billing but complicates edge proxies. late-join keeps flexibility but creates gaps for short-lived requests.

Dmitri P.: Can we do a probabilistic fuzzy-match as a soft fallback? e.g. if billing_key missing, match on (tenant_id, span_root_hash, 10s window) with a confidence score. Not perfect, but covers most `short-lived` traces.

Sarah L.: I'm wary. Fuzzy-match means billing could be non-deterministic and customers will ask for guarantees. We need a clear SLA: fuzzy-match is only for best-effort monthly rollups, never for invoices or chargebacks.

Kevin R.: Agreed on SLA. Operationally, fuzzy-match also needs a circuit-breaker: if match rate < X or mismatch rate > Y, stop using it and surface alerts. Otherwise we silently leak cost.

Maria G.: Proposal: 3-tier approach
1) prefer explicit billing_key if present (no change)
2) if missing, attempt attribute resolution via late-join lookup in attribute-store (synchronous, TTL 5s)
3) if lookup fails, run fuzzy-match heuristic and attach metadata field `cost_resolution=best_effort` with `confidence=0.XX`

Ben T.: That seems reasonable. A few tradeoffs: (2) adds tail latency to ingest path ~p95 +12ms. We can mitigate with async backfill: ingest accepts placeholder, and async job attaches billing_key when available — but query-time joins then need to handle backfilled rows.

Dmitri P.: Implementation note: store fuzzy-match candidates in a small LRU index keyed by (tenant_id, recent_root_hashes). We already have an LRU per shard for routing; reuse it. Pseudocode:```
if (!billing_key) {
  candidate = attribute_store.lookup(trace_id)
  if (candidate) attach(candidate)
  else {
    match = lru.fuzzy_match(tenant_id, span_root_hash)
    if (match) attach({billing_key: match.k, cost_resolution: "best_effort", confidence: match.score})
  }
}
```

Sarah L.: Add telemetry: emit `cost_attrib.path` = {explicit, late_lookup, fuzzy} and counters for `fuzzy_mismatch` when customer-supplied audit disagrees. That helps iterate.

Kevin R.: Rollout plan: feature-flag the fuzzy-match per-region. Start in staging for 72h, run side-by-side with strict-mode to collect discrepancy metrics. If fuzzy false positives > 0.5% for 24h, rollback.

Maria G.: Also need query semantics doc update: explain `cost_resolution` field and how to exclude best_effort rows. Docs PR incoming.

Ben T.: One more: privacy. Ensure fuzzy-match uses only non-PII keys (tenant_id, hashed_root). No customer PII used for matching. Confirmed?

Dmitri P.: Confirmed. We use SHA256(root_id) truncated. No raw IDs shared across shards.

deploy-bot: Deployment plan published: eng-platform/cost-attrib/fuzzy-flag -> canary -> staged rollout. Runbook: if `fuzzy_mismatch > 0.5%` auto-toggle off.

Sarah L.: Action items: (1) Dmitri implement LRU index + metrics (2) Ben wire feature-flag + circuit-breaker (3) Maria update docs + SLA note (4) Kevin own rollout and runbook. I'll draft the PR template for audits.

Maria G.: Thanks team. I'll open an RFC follow-up note summarizing decisions and link the rollout tickets. :thumbsup:

Ben T.: Ping me when PRs reference the canary ticket, I'll review quick.

Dmitri P.: Starting prototyping now, will post perf numbers by EOD tomorrow.

Sarah L.: Putting a calendar reminder for a post-canary review next week.

Kevin R.: Sounds good.
